projects.title: Raceway USA
projects.short: A road-trip mini golf adventure built through hands-on construction and scenic painting.
projects.coverAlt: Raceway USA scenic course in the workshop, with miniature buildings, a Ferris wheel, and Las Vegas scenery
projects.overview: Raceway USA is a road-trip-themed, nine-hole mini golf course built around playful elements of sabotage at every hole. As part of CTIN-295 Project Crew, I worked on the construction and painting side of the project, helping bring two themed holes—Aspen and New Orleans—from the design team's direction into physical environments.
projects.role: I worked with a team of four on two holes. For Aspen, I helped construct the platform. For New Orleans, I built and painted the shotgun houses and created a ceramic horse statue. The design team provided direction on what needed to be made, while giving me creative freedom in figuring out how to make it. My construction work primarily used wood, saws, nail guns, screws, wood glue, and other building materials.

sections.title: Building two road-trip destinations
sections.text: Working with three other teammates, I contributed to the physical build of the Aspen and New Orleans holes. My work on Aspen focused on constructing its platform. For New Orleans, I created and painted the shotgun houses and made a ceramic horse statue, adding handmade scenic details to the themed environment.
images: Raceway USA · Horse sculpture, front view
Raceway USA · Horse sculpture, side view

sections.title: From design direction to the physical build
sections.text: The design team identified what each hole needed, then gave our construction team creative freedom in deciding how to make it. I worked primarily with wood and standard shop tools and materials, including saws, nail guns, screws, and wood glue, to translate those ideas into physical pieces.

sections.title: Lessons carried into the next course
sections.text: Raceway USA showed me how important communication and teamwork are to creating a cohesive visual style across a course. It also reinforced that scenic ideas have to work as mini golf: the mechanics of the golf ball matter, and obstacles and surfaces need to support how the game is actually played. These lessons informed the way our team approached the later Outlaw City project.

projects.title: As the Trees Grow
projects.subtitle: A Fairy Tale Parade
projects.course: CTIN 455 · Designing with Specialists for Themed Entertainment
projects.coverAlt: As the Trees Grow: A Fairy Tale Parade presentation cover with a forest illustration
projects.overview: A collaborative parade concept inspired by Grimm’s fairy tales. Seven story-inspired floats bring together performance, music, costumes, and puppetry around a shared theme: venturing into the unknown to gain self-determination.
projects.role: Collaborative USC coursework. Individual contributions and complete team credits will be added once confirmed.

sections.title: Enter the forest
sections.text: The concept moves through The Pied Piper, Rumpelstiltskin, Little Red Riding Hood, Rapunzel, the Town Musicians of Bremen, Hansel and Gretel, and The Twelve Dancing Princesses. Scenic and performance references help establish a common woodland world.

projects.title: Yellow Submarine
projects.subtitle: Bar & Lounge

projects.overview: An immersive, psychedelic cocktail-bar concept inspired by The Beatles’ Yellow Submarine. The experience invites adult guests to leave the everyday behind and enter an underwater world shaped by music, color, and a sequence of imaginative spaces.
projects.role: Developed by Silvia Schohn, Jenna Bortnick, and Zoe Reynolds. Original concept by Connor Nanus and Nayeli Castillo. Jenna’s individual responsibilities are being confirmed.

sections.title: Sail to sea
sections.text: A space walkthrough, musical references, and a themed menu connect the bar’s physical setting to its larger story. These are selected pages from the collaborative concept pitch.

projects.title: Ibiza Skylink
projects.short: A new perspective on getting there.
projects.coverAlt: Ibiza Skylink title slide with yellow lettering over a coastal scene
projects.overview: A suspended-train concept connecting Ibiza’s nightlife, beaches, and airport, with a journey as vibrant as the destination. The collaborative pitch explores how an attraction could address visitor transportation while becoming part of the island experience, from daytime coastal views to colorful nighttime journeys.
projects.role: Developed by Silvia Schohn, Jenna Bortnick, and Jasmine Wan. Original concept by Silvia Schohn and Sammy Hillery. Jenna’s individual responsibilities are being confirmed.

sections.title: Connecting day and night
sections.text: The presentation maps daytime attractions, nightlife destinations, the airport, and existing road connections to frame the transportation challenge. These maps document research for the course concept.
images: Ibiza by day and night · Destination research
Attraction and airport map · Team presentation

sections.title: A journey worth taking
sections.text: The proposal treats transportation as an attraction in its own right. Suspended-rail precedents and colorful vehicle references inform possibilities for the guest experience.
images: Theming references · Hospitality and themed vehicles

sections.title: Along the route
sections.text: Concept visuals explore suspended trains in coastal and nightlife settings. Destination photographs and interior references establish the atmosphere of the proposed experience.

sections.title: Room to grow
sections.text: The academic proposal considers taking visitors off the roads, managing crowds, and making travel more accessible. VIP cars and local pop-ups extend the concept. Fares and operating benefits shown in the slides are proposal assumptions, not a live transport service.

projects.title: Blue Horizon
projects.coverAlt: Blue Horizon title in turquoise and gold on a deep blue background
projects.overview: A steampunk submarine adventure conceived as an interactive escape-room experience aboard a cruise ship. A crew of four to eight guests journeys through a fantasy world of treasure, puzzles, and a kraken encounter, with the experience developed through story, guest flow, spatial planning, and show elements.
projects.role: Jenna is credited for the floorplan design. Collaborative project by Jenna Bortnick, Christy Li, Sam Ruttenberg, and Ryan Rosendahl; other individual responsibilities are being confirmed.

sections.title: Story meets spatial design
sections.text: The floorplan organizes the experience into parallel paths through engine rooms, navigation decks, captain’s quarters, and a finale. Selected presentation pages show the connection between narrative beats and the guest journey.
images: Engine-room puzzle development · Artwork by Christy Li

projects.title: Traveling Escape Room
projects.short: Taking the experience on the road.
projects.course: CTIN 457 · Business of Themed Entertainment Final
projects.coverAlt: Traveling Escape Room Feasibility presentation cover
projects.overview: A collaborative feasibility study for a traveling escape-room experience operating in major cities. The project considers what it takes to move a themed attraction from an idea into a workable business, connecting the visitor experience with operations, logistics, and financial assumptions.
projects.role: Group project by Jenna, Amandine, Charlie, Silvia, and Kalia. Individual responsibilities are being confirmed. Financial material represents an academic model, not actual operating results.

sections.title: Behind the experience
sections.text: The study examines city selection, space and capacity, staffing, transportation, intellectual-property considerations, capital costs, and sensitivity testing. The selected slides document the team’s planning approach.

projects.title: Outlaw City
projects.short: A nine-hole outlaw adventure, designed as an immersive mini golf experience.
projects.course: CTIN-395: Mini Golf Design · Collaborative design & build project
projects.coverAlt: Outlaw City digital environment layout in Blender
projects.overview: Outlaw City reimagines traditional mini golf as an immersive, story-driven adventure. Players are invited to try out for Pecos Bill’s outlaw gang, proving themselves through a series of nine trials. Developed collaboratively by our cohort, the project brings together storytelling, gameplay, spatial design, digital modeling, and plans for hands-on construction.
projects.role: Working collaboratively with my cohort, I contribute to gameplay development, course layout, 3D modeling, and planning for the physical build. My primary focus is the overall course footprint and spatial arrangement, as well as the placement of the nine holes and individual hole models in Blender. I also lead meetings, track progress, and coordinate communication between the art and gameplay teams so everyone understands current decisions, responsibilities, and how the work fits together.

sections.title: From mini golf to an immersive adventure
sections.text: The concept begins with a question: how can mini golf become more than nine separate holes? In Outlaw City, players are invited to try out for Pecos Bill’s outlaw gang. Each hole becomes a trial on the path to proving yourself as an outlaw, connecting the gameplay to a larger story and themed world.

sections.title: Designing for the SCI Lawn
sections.text: The course is being developed for the SCI Lawn, a designated site with existing conditions that shape the design. Slopes, trees, and perimeter lights all influence the available footprint and the placement of the nine holes. Our team is using a site plan, measured dimensions, and a 3D scan of the lawn to understand the space and make informed layout decisions. My focus is bringing the course together as a cohesive plan while considering circulation, gameplay, and buildability.

sections.title: Developing holes, gameplay & models
sections.text: We are brainstorming individual hole concepts, sketching layouts, developing gameplay mechanics, and building digital models. I use Blender to work on both the placement of the holes across the site and the individual hole models. Our team also uses Rhino, sharing software-specific responsibilities according to each person's experience. As the designs develop, we are evaluating how the digital models can translate into physical construction.

sections.title: Collaboration, coordination & the build ahead
sections.text: Alongside my design work, I lead meetings, track progress, and coordinate between the art and gameplay teams to keep communication clear and everyone informed. The project has reinforced how much time creative and construction tasks can take, and how important realistic planning and consistent communication are to keeping a collaborative project moving. The course is still in development; the next phase will bring the designs into hands-on construction, where I plan to contribute primarily to the build and, hopefully, additional coordination.
